authorizedBy: founder directive 2026-07-31 (board truth programme, phase 2: the columns are yours; full execution authorization given in-session)
authorizationSource: operator session instruction: retire the waiting raw-text lane at source — rewrite lane on existing rows and seed the column config for affected workspaces; production counts measured via the db-migrate measure command before execution

migrations.risk: medium (three-statement data rewrite; no schema change, no row deleted). Statement 1 inserts configs only where none exist; statement 2 appends a JSON member only to configs that lack the quoted waiting key; statement 3 rewrites lane='waiting' rows to a board_column_key claim with the canonical doing lane. The application resolves the claim and the raw text to the same column, so surfaces render identically before, during and after.
migrations.rollbackPlan: UPDATE tasks SET lane = 'waiting', board_column_key = NULL WHERE board_column_key = 'waiting' AND lane = 'doing' restores the pre-migration row shape for every row this migration touched (rows a user later moves are indistinguishable and stay where the user put them); seeded configs are inert under the old code and can be deleted by key. The workflow's verified backup restores the exact prior state if a full revert is ever preferred.
postconditions: no task row holds the raw lane text 'waiting'
every waiting claim sits on the canonical doing lane
no non-canonical lane text remains at all
every workspace holding waiting claims has a column config that names the waiting key

proofs.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM tasks WHERE lane = 'waiting'
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM tasks WHERE board_column_key = 'waiting' AND lane <> 'doing'
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM tasks WHERE lane NOT IN ('todo','doing','review','done')

SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM (SELECT DISTINCT t.workspace_id FROM tasks t WHERE t.board_column_key = 'waiting' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM meta m WHERE m.key = 'board:' || t.workspace_id || ':columns' AND m.value LIKE '%"waiting"%'))
SELECT integrity_check AS value FROM pragma_integrity_check
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM pragma_foreign_key_check
